section_1.title: Intuitive Hook: The Speedometer and the GPS
section_1.content: Introduce the concept of 'Rate of Change' vs. 'Accumulation'. Use a visual of a car: The speedometer shows instantaneous speed (derivative), while the GPS tracking history shows total distance traveled (integral).
section_1.example: A cat running: Its current speed at any moment is the derivative of its position; the total ground covered over time is the integral of that speed curve.

section_2.title: The Geometric Connection
section_2.content: Establish the prerequisite: The slope of a tangent line (derivative) vs. the area under a curve (integral). Visualize a bar chart evolving into a smooth curve, showing that as the width of rectangles approaches zero, the sum becomes an integral.
section_2.example: Visualizing the area under a velocity-time graph as the total displacement of a robot arm.

section_3.title: The Fundamental Theorem of Calculus (Part I)
section_3.content: Define the relationship: If you accumulate the rate of change of a function, you return to the original function. Provide the formal visualization: The area function A(x) changes at a rate equal to the height of the curve f(x).
section_3.example: The 'Water Tank' analogy: The rate at which water flows into a tank (f(x)) is the derivative of the total volume of water in the tank (A(x)).

section_4.title: The Inverse Operation: Differentiation and Integration
section_4.content: Explain that integration and differentiation are inverse processes, similar to multiplication and division. Show a flowchart: F(x) --(diff)--> f(x) --(int)--> F(x) + C.
section_4.example: A balloon being inflated: The rate of change of the radius (derivative) determines the growth of the volume, and integrating that growth rate recovers the volume function.

section_5.title: Summary and Synthesis
section_5.content: Conclude by highlighting the power of this relationship: It allows us to calculate areas of complex, irregular shapes using simple algebraic formulas (antiderivatives).
section_5.example: Calculating the precise surface area of a uniquely shaped dragon wing by integrating the curvature function derived from its profile.

        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2

section_1.title: Intuitive Hook: The Speedometer and the GPS
lecture_lines: Speedometer shows instantaneous speed: the derivative.
GPS history tracks distance: the integral.
Two faces of motion, linked by time.
animations: Display a [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/speedometer.svg] with a [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/needle.svg] pointing at varying speeds (#FFFFFF).

Highlight the correlation between speed and position change (#00FF00).

section_2.title: The Geometric Connection
lecture_lines: Tangent slope defines the derivative.
Area under curves defines the integral.
Small rectangles sum to the total area.
animations: Visualize a curve on a plane (#FFFFFF) using a [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/ruler.svg] to measure the axes.
Show the area under the curve as a filling rectangle (#00FFFF).
Demonstrate slicing the area into tiny strips (#FFCC00).
Animate the strips summing to the total area (#AA00FF).
Show the relationship between slope and growth rate (#FFFFFF) using a [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/calculator.svg] to compute the values.

section_3.title: The Fundamental Theorem of Calculus (Part I)
lecture_lines: Accumulating rate returns the original function.
Volume growth is the rate of flow.
The area function's rate is the curve.
Fundamental Theorem links accumulation and change.
Integration undoes differentiation's work.
animations: Define a function f(t) representing velocity (#FFFFFF). [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/speedometer.svg]
Represent the integral as an accumulating area function (#00FFFF).

from manim import *
import numpy as np

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (6x6 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                # Adjusted grid coordinates to accommodate column 3 as a buffer
                x = 1.0 + j * 0.9
                y = 2.0 - i * 0.8
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject
